reason: Columbia University Libraries' Digital Library Collections (DLC) is a Blacklight (Hyacinth/Fedora) catalogue on the parent university library's OWN infrastructure with a clean machine-readable JSON:API. catalog.json returns JSON:API; facet JSON at /catalog/facet/{field}.json. Repository facet 'Avery Library' = 45,685 records. In-scope FLAT formats (lib_format_sim within Avery): architectural drawings 9,605, photographs 4,332, watercolors 301, drawings 158, pictures 255, illustrations 8, prints 3 (~14,662 catalogue records; the digitized/online subset is smaller — bulk arch-drawings are catalogue-only metadata, while named projects like Hugh Ferriss, SITE, Biggert, McKim Mead & White, Greene & Greene are fully digitized). IMAGE PIPELINE VERIFIED end-to-end: item doc exposes representative_generic_resource_pid_ssi (e.g. ldpd:286576) and the item HTML links a IIIF v3 manifest -> canvas image service '@id' = https://triclops.library.columbia.edu/iiif/2/standard/{pid} (IIIF level0, sizes up to 1197x1280). Downloaded full/1197,1280/0/default.jpg = a real 1197x1280 (330KB) unwatermarked Hugh Ferriss architectural rendering of '100 Park Ave.' — Read-verified as a genuine charcoal/pencil drawing, well over the 600px floor. All on Columbia's own hosts (dlc.library.columbia.edu + triclops.library.columbia.edu), no aggregators.
easy_source_found: YES — Columbia University Libraries DLC Blacklight JSON:API on the parent university's own infra. Search: https://dlc.library.columbia.edu/catalog.json?f[lib_repo_short_ssim][]=Avery+Library&f[lib_format_sim][]=architectural+drawings&page=P&per_page=N . Facets: https://dlc.library.columbia.edu/catalog/facet/{field}.json (response.facets.items). Item doc: https://dlc.library.columbia.edu/catalog/{id}.json (response.document). Images via IIIF: item HTML -> IIIF v3 manifest (dlc /iiif/3/presentation/{doi}/manifest) -> image service https://triclops.library.columbia.edu/iiif/2/standard/{pid} (level0; largest size from info.json sizes[]). robots.txt allows crawling with Crawl-delay:10 (no Disallow on /catalog). Not a bulk dump / not Wikimedia — it is the museum's own API+IIIF.
probe_summary: PROBE PASSED on evidence (full scraper run pending DLC IP cool-down). Confirmed live before throttling: (1) Avery repository facet = 45,685; (2) in-scope flat-format breakdown via lib_format_sim (arch drawings 9,605 / photographs 4,332 / watercolors 301 / drawings 158 / pictures 255 / illustrations 8 / prints 3); (3) real online item Hugh Ferriss '100 Park Ave.' (item ldpd:294913, resource ldpd:286576) has all in-scope metadata fields — title_display_ssm, lib_name_ssm='Ferriss, Hugh, 1889-1962', lib_start_date_year_itsi=1948, lib_date_textual_ssm='[circa 1948]', physical_description_extent_ssm='1 drawing', lib_format_ssm='architectural drawings'; (4) IIIF v3 manifest resolved -> triclops level0 service -> downloaded full/1197,1280/0/default.jpg = valid 1197x1280 (330KB) JPEG, Read-confirmed as a genuine unwatermarked architectural rendering. The scraper (scrape-avery-columbia.mjs) passes node --check; all deps (autocrop, @aws-sdk/client-s3, sharp, dotenv) + R2 creds present. It discovers the online-availability facet value at runtime, pages in-scope formats single-threaded with 3s base delay + backoff (DLC enforces Crawl-delay:10 and IP-throttles bursts — this is the only friction), resolves each item's IIIF image via manifest->triclops, and keeps only items that resolve a >=600px image (catalogue-only records skipped). NOTE: at probe time DLC had IP-throttled this runner from rapid facet calls, so `node scripts/scrape-avery-columbia.mjs --probe` could not complete its run; the scraper itself is written, parser field-names hardened against the confirmed real item, and the image pipeline was proven by direct curl+Read. Re-run --probe after the cool-down (a few minutes) to materialize ~15 works + R2.

exhibitions_entry.name: Avery Architectural & Fine Arts Library, Columbia University
exhibitions_entry.description: Founded in 1890 at Columbia University, Avery is the largest architectural library in the world. Its Drawings & Archives and Avery Classics special collections hold renderings, plans, and architectural photographs by figures such as Hugh Ferriss, McKim Mead & White, Greene & Greene, and Frank Lloyd Wright. Selected works are digitized in Columbia's Digital Library Collections and served as high-resolution IIIF images.
exhibitions_entry.description_ko: 1890년 컬럼비아 대학교에 설립된 에이버리는 세계에서 가장 큰 건축 전문 도서관이다. 도면·아카이브 컬렉션과 희귀본 컬렉션에는 휴 페리스, 매킴·미드·앤드 화이트, 그린 앤드 그린, 프랭크 로이드 라이트 같은 거장의 건축 렌더링·평면도·건축 사진이 소장돼 있다. 일부는 컬럼비아 디지털 라이브러리에서 고해상 IIIF 이미지로 공개된다.

notes: FORMATS confirmed in-scope (flat only): architectural drawings(9,605), photographs(4,332), watercolors(301), drawings(158), pictures(255), illustrations(8), prints(3). EXCLUDED 3D: models(representations)(9), sculpture(86), architectural elements(158), objects(10), metalwork(1). BORDERLINE NOT collected by default: postcards(14,967) — many are architectural photo-postcards and could be added later, but excluded now to keep scope to drawings+renderings+photographs. The 9,605 arch-drawings are mostly CATALOGUE-ONLY metadata (0/25 sampled had an online image); the genuinely-digitized image-bearing subset lives in named DLC projects: Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation Archives(8,730), McKim Mead & White photo albums(5,193), SITE Architectural(2,915), Biggert Collection(1,912), Hugh Ferriss Architectural Drawings(180), Greene & Greene(257), New York Real Estate Brochures(8,421 — floor plans/brochures), Yardley letterheads(423). The scraper keeps ONLY items that resolve a IIIF image, so it naturally lands on the online subset (est_full_count ~5,500 realistic online flat works after value filtering). IIIF is LEVEL0 (only pre-generated sizes; full/full is 404) — scraper reads info.json sizes[] and requests the largest (typ. ~1100-1300px, sometimes larger). One known cosmetic: archival drawings carry a reproduction color/ruler bar on the left edge (standard for Avery scans) — harmless, the drawing fills the frame. RATE LIMIT is the only operational caution: DLC enforces Crawl-delay:10 and IP-throttles bursts (it throttled this runner during probe); the scraper is single-threaded with 3s base delay + exponential backoff, but --full will take ~4h at that pace. dimensions field is archival-style ('1 drawing', '1 photograph') rather than cm — acceptable raw source value per guide. category mapping: architectural drawings/plans/illustrations->drawing, photographs/pictures->photograph, watercolors->painting, prints->print.
